For presenters

Program 1

Song and Dance

Dvořák's American summer and the Schumanns' Leipzig: two quartets, a quintet and three romances.

Warmth, lyricism, and rhythmic vitality bring together the music of Dvořák and the Schumanns. A flute arrangement of Dvořák's beloved "American" Quartet lends a fresh colour to its expansive melodies and spirited exchanges, before Robert Schumann's Piano Quartet draws us into a world of tenderness and Romantic intensity. After the intermission, Clara Schumann's Three Romances offer a moment of intimate reflection. Dvořák's Piano Quintet No. 2 brings the evening to an exuberant close, balancing songful expression with the irresistible energy of dance.

  • Antonín DvořákString Quartet No. 12 in F major, Op. 96, "American" (arrangement with flute) 24'
  • Robert SchumannPiano Quartet in E-flat major, Op. 47 25'
  • Intermission
  • Clara SchumannThree Romances, Op. 22 9'
  • Antonín DvořákPiano Quintet No. 2 in A major, Op. 81 40'

Music, about 98 minutes, with one intermission.

Program 2

Fairy Tales and Fairgrounds

French colour and Hungarian invention, ending in Stravinsky's fairground.

Ravel's luminous sound world meets the bold imagination of Hungarian composers György Kurtág and György Ligeti in a first half shaped by contrast and discovery. The delicate fairy-tale scenes of Ma mère l'Oye sit alongside the concentrated gestures of Kurtág's Tre pezzi and the rhythmic wit of Ligeti's Musica ricercata, creating a dialogue between French colour and Hungarian invention. Ravel's Kaddish offers an expressive moment of contemplation before the intermission. Stravinsky's Petrushka then opens the door to a vivid carnival world, bringing the evening to a close with bustling dances, theatrical drama, and dazzling musical contrasts.

  • Maurice RavelMa mère l'Oye 16'
  • György KurtágTre pezzi 7'
  • György LigetiMusica ricercata 15'
  • Maurice RavelKaddish 5'
  • Intermission
  • Igor StravinskyPetrushka 40'

Music, about 83 minutes, with one intermission.

This programme · PDF ↓

Both programmes can be adapted to suit different concert lengths. CreArtBox tours as a piano quintet - flute, piano, violin, viola and cello - and builds separate programmes for smaller formations: this season a piano trio goes to Illinois and a flute, cello and piano programme to the Hudson Valley. For a programme built around a theme, an anniversary or a local commission, write to info@creartbox.nyc: the ensemble has played everything listed here, and reads new scores every season through its open call. Fees on request, by formation and date.

The ensembleAbout CreArtBox.

CreArtBox creates and produces live art performances, fusing classical and contemporary music with original ideas encouraged by multidisciplinary interaction, and works to make world-class performances accessible to everyone regardless of background or economic circumstance.

Recognized by The New Yorker as one of its "art and music top picks," praised by Time Out as "an ensemble devoted to multidisciplinary events," and described by BroadwayWorld as "wholly authentic, visually and aurally compelling," the ensemble is known for enhancing the listening experience of live music through theatrical design while preserving the integrity of each composition.

It was founded in New York City in 2013 by flutist Guillermo Laporta and pianist Josefina Urraca, who continue as its artistic directors, and is now in its 12th season; the project was originally conceived in Europe in 2006 as Cre.Art Project. With headquarters in New York City and Asturias, Spain, CreArtBox gives its New York Series at The DiMenna Center for Classical Music, tours internationally, and runs a printed magazine, a streaming platform, a live music podcast, an open call and commissioning program for composers, and Festival ADAR in rural Spain.

The performance that most defines its identity is the visual concert, in which visual art and theatrical design surround live classical and contemporary music; the ensemble also plays traditional chamber programs, which have taken it to Japan, Spain, Europe, Canada and the east coast of the United States.

An open Call for Scores has run since the first season, bringing works by Pulitzer Prize winners and emerging composers alike into the programmes. CreArtBox is supported by the New York State Council on the Arts, the NYC Department of Cultural Affairs, the Amphion Foundation, the Alice M. Ditson Fund and the Aaron Copland Fund for Music, among others.
